newsitem.title: INDIA: India slams alleged Pakistani attack on diplomat.
newsitem.headline: India slams alleged Pakistani attack on diplomat.

text.p: India has condemned an alleged attack on one of its personnel in Islamabad during an apparent tit-for-tat expulsion of diplomatic staff accused of spying, the Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency said on Sunday.
It quoted official sources as saying that New Delhi would express to Islamabad its serious concern over the alleged attack on Ashok Kumar Wahi on Saturday.
Indian officials could not be reached for comment.

PTI quoted the sources as saying the Indian government was appalled at the harm done to Wahi and his wife who Indian officials say were subjected to physical and knife attacks by Pakistan's intelligence agents.
Islamabad expelled Wahi after police detained him while he was meeting an alleged contact on behalf of the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), India's intelligence unit.
It said Wahi had confessed he was a spy who offered money for sensitive information.

India saw the expulsion as a retaliation for its own expulsion of Hafiz Ahmed Khosa, who was held on Friday as he was alleged to have accepted secret documents on the Indian navy from an Indian student, Ravinder Kumar.
Indian police arrested Kumar under official secret laws.

An Indian high commission spokesman in Islamabad had dismissed the charge against Wahi as baseless and said a dozen men wielding knives and a revolver had broken into Wahi's home and forcibly taken him away on Saturday.
His wife suffered a knife wound on the hand and his teenaged daughter was badly shaken up, the spokesman said.

Pakistan's high commission said in New Delhi that Khosa was abducted and framed by Indian intelligence agents. "He was also physically beaten up at the police station and forced to make a confessional statement," it said on Saturday.
